
=================================================================
#5 Eight Great Clans  (632)
Arc: Part I — The Three Kingdoms / The King for All · place: sabi · tone: clan face-off (shonen)
Logline: Satek. Yunbi. Jinmo. Mokli. Hae. Baek. Guk. Ahn.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ Satek. Yunbi. Jinmo. Mokli. Hae. Baek. Guk. Ahn.
[1] ¶ The Eight Great Clans run this country, and one king sits between them. Today, on the crown prince’s day, they settle nothing on the sand. They never do.
[2] [TERM Eight Great Clans (大姓八族): The eight great surnames. Not a council and not a party. Eight families, each older than most kings, each with a seat on the rock, a berth on the river and a grudge against at least two of the others. The royal Buyeo house sits above them. Usually.]
[3] ¶ The Chinese wrote the eight names down too, and got half of them wrong. That tells you how often the clans let outsiders count them.
[4] ❝QUOTE (Sui Shu (隋書) bk. 81, Eastern Barbarians — Baekje): The great surnames of the country are eight clans: Sa, Yeon, Hyeop, Hae, Jin, Guk, Mok and Baek.❞
[5] ── SCENE: The Sand ──
[6] ¶ On the crown prince’s day, the court chalks a square grid in the palace yard. Four hard lines. No banners. The young men of each house step onto the grid in white.
[7] 🗣: The Yunbi boys turned a Satek cart over at the west bridge yesterday. / Then tonight the Satek go over a Yunbi wall. / Same as the lantern festival last year. / Last year three of them died.
[8] Elder Satek: White cloth. Wooden swords. / If anyone bleeds the wrong colour, the harbour talks stop for a month.
[9] [CARD Elder Yunbi: Head of the Yunbi. The family business is knowing things first.]
[10] Elder Yunbi: Then keep your boys’ wrists honest. / The chalk does not care whose sleeve they hold.
[11] ¶ Swords first. Wooden ones, which still remember steel. The Jinmo boy holds his blade high over his head, the Jinmo way, daring you. A Hae boy takes the dare. On the call they both move. Blades skim the chalk. The white sleeves clap together so close that the steps gasp.
[12] 🗣: That Jinmo boy? / Fast wrists. / Faster feet than the Hae, too. / Point to Jinmo.
[13] ¶ The Jinmo boy bows to the steps and looks straight past the Hae boy, to the edge of the sand, where the crown prince’s nobody is waiting.
[14] ¶ When the wooden points are tallied, the sand comes out. A circle of grit inside the same square. Ssireum — satba locked before they stand, knees in the grit, equal grips on waist and thigh, then up without letting go. No circling for a hold. The bout is the hold.
[15] ¶ A Yunbi boy hooks a leg, low, the coast-road way. The Satek boy answers with his hip. He lifts, he turns, and the Yunbi boy’s feet leave the earth. The yard goes quiet the way a dock goes quiet when a rope snaps. Sand takes the shoulder. The chalk does not argue.
[16] Elder Satek: See? / Even Yunbi can fall without a cart.
[17] Elder Yunbi: Your boy’s knee touched first. / Ask the chalk.
[18] ¶ The elders watch from the hall steps. They always do, and they still count wrong when it is their sleeve.
[19] ── SCENE: The Last Bout ──
[20] ¶ Last on the sand: the Jinmo boy, and the crown prince’s nobody. For five days the Jinmo boy has told the steps what he will do to a peasant. Now the peasant has a royal surname, and the steps want to see.
[21] The Jinmo Boy: Buyeo. BUYEO. / You got that name off a drunk on a riverbank, eel boy. I’ll hand it back to him in pieces.
[22] Gyebek: It was given.
[23] The Jinmo Boy: …What?
[24] Gyebek: You said I got it. It was given. That is different.
[25] ¶ Satba. Equal grips, knees in the grit, then up together. The Jinmo boy is a head taller, and he knows it. He leans.
[26] 🗣: Jinmo’s got him— / Look at the eel boy’s feet, he’s going— / He’s not going anywhere. Look.
[27] ¶ Gyebek’s heels slide back a finger’s width, and stop. He does not try to throw. He holds, the way he held a rope in a river for five days, and he waits.
[28] King Euija: Ha! Look at him, Father. He isn’t wrestling. / He’s waiting for the other one to get bored of breathing.
[29] King Mu: Sit down. You’ll frighten the Satek.
[30] The Jinmo Boy: Let— go— you—
[31] Gyebek: No.
[32] ¶ The Jinmo boy runs out of breath first. Gyebek turns him the way you turn over a full basket: carefully, so nothing spills.
[33] ¶ Sand takes a Jinmo shoulder. On the royal steps, a crown prince with no interest in clan quarrels is on his feet.
[34] ¶ Then someone in the crowd starts the old chant, the one every house in Sabi knows by heart, because a royal name has just won on the sand. Eraha is the old Baekje word for king.
[35] 🗣: Restore the reign of the thirteenth Eraha!
[36] ¶ Euija hears it and stops smiling. Nobody notices, except Gyebek, who is still on his knees in the sand and looking straight at him.
[37] ¶ By dusk the white is grey with chalk and grit. Nobody has settled four generations of anything. The throne likes it that way. The boys go home with a score instead of a funeral.
[38] ── SCENE: The Assembly ──
[39] ¶ In the Assembly they fight for power, each house holding a share of the king's sons. They fight in the street too. Same fight. The street version is older.
[40] [TERM Rock of Politics (政事巖): The Rock of Government. Long ago Baekje’s lords chose their premier by sealing three names in a box and leaving it on this rock overnight. Whichever name the rock had marked by morning got the chair. The rock still sweats before a vote. The votes still go to whoever paid for them.]
[41] ¶ Unlike Silla’s Harmony Council, the Assembly does not require every voice. A plurality of houses is enough — which is why the street fights matter. Votes can be bought in pieces. In Surabol they must be bought entire, or not at all.
[42] ¶ What the Assembly votes on, more often than war, is water. Who loads first. Whose ships winter in the river mouth. Who gets the orange levy, and who gets the silk berth. In this country, a clan without a harbour can't feed a fight.
[43] Elder Satek: Yunbi talks of blood. / We talk of berths. / Blood cools. A winter anchorage does not.
[44] Elder Yunbi: You hold the king’s sleeve and call it a harbour. / We don’t hold the sleeve. We hold the arm.
[45] ¶ **Satek** and **Yunbi** have been at it for four generations. Nobody alive can say what started it. Everybody alive can list the last six things.
[46] ¶ Today, for once, they agree on something. They don’t like the boy on the sand.
[47] Elder Satek: Buyeo, on an eel boy. / Every house on this rock owns one of the crown prince’s sons. Now he has a man none of us own.
[48] Elder Yunbi: Then we buy him. Before you do.
[49] Elder Satek: You’ll overpay. You always do.
[50] ¶ Neither house has ever won, and nothing about that is accidental: the throne needs both of them standing. A clan with no rival starts watching the throne.
[51] 🗣: They say Yunbi already knows what was said in the Satek meeting. / And Satek already knows the Yunbi one. / So both know, and both pretend not to. / That’s politics.
[52] ── SCENE: The Rock at Dusk ──
[53] ¶ When the rock is empty, the crown prince is still sitting on it, which is not allowed. His new man stands beside him, which is not allowed either.
[54] King Euija: They want to buy you, you know. Both of them. They’ll bid all winter.
[55] Gyebek: I am not for sale.
[56] King Euija: Ha! No. That’s what frightens them. / You heard the chant on the sand?
[57] Gyebek: Yes. Everyone knows it.
[58] King Euija: Do you know what it’s about?
[59] Gyebek: No.
[60] King Euija: Neither do they. That’s the trouble. / Eight houses, one river, and the only thing they’ll shout together is a king three hundred years dead. / This country needs a new story, Gyebek. The old one is wearing out.
[61] Gyebek: Who will tell it?
[62] ¶ Euija laughs, and does not answer, which for him is a kind of answer.
[63] ¶ **Why is one dead king the only thing eight houses still agree on? To find out, we go back three hundred years…!**
